transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, and I don't want to take up too much of your time. I'm a transportation inspector, and... well, I'm here mostly because I've been dealing with some stress at the office, and I want to make sure I'm handling things the right way. Does that make sense? 

It's just... ever since I got this county safety award a little while back—which was a huge honor, I always try to do my best—it just feels like certain people at work have been... well, twisting my inspection reports. And they keep asking me these really pointed budget questions, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked or something. I brought it up to my supervisor, and he says it’s just a normal review process. I really want to be a team player and believe him, I do, but... I don't know, I can just tell there’s some kind of coordinated effort to discredit me. I hope I don't sound unreasonable saying that. Am I explaining that okay?

Can you tell me more about these feelings that people are trying to discredit you? Have you noticed any specific behaviors or evidence that support these thoughts, or do they happen even when there's no clear proof?

Well, um, I really don't want to come across as... you know, someone who complains or can't take constructive feedback. I always try to be professional and do things by the book. Is it okay if I explain how it started? 

It was right after I won that county safety award. I thought everyone was happy for me, but then... certain people at work started taking my inspection reports and, well, twisting the wording around. And then they’d pull me aside and ask these really pointed budget questions. They're just... phrased in a way to make me look crooked, if that makes sense? 

I really don't want to think badly of my coworkers. I hate even bringing it up because I don't want you to think I'm just making excuses or being difficult. When I went to my supervisor about it, he assured me it was just a normal review process. I smiled and agreed with him because I want to be a good employee, but... deep down, even with him saying that, I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I know how that sounds, and I really hope you don't judge me for saying it. I just... I can feel it happening. Am I explaining that clearly enough for you?
Do these feelings that people are trying to discredit you happen only at work, or do you feel this way in other parts of your life too, like with family, friends, or in other situations?

Um, no, it's... it really is just at work. I try very hard to not let it affect the rest of my life, you know? I want to make sure I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do. 

I mean, I still get to work on time every day, and I complete all my inspections just like I always have. I haven't missed church on Sundays, and I make sure I'm taking care of myself at home, keeping things tidy and all that. I really pride myself on being responsible. 

It's really only... well, the main problems only come up when people at the office bring up those specific reports, or when they start questioning my spending. That's when I get that feeling. But with my family and friends, everything is fine. I hope that shows that I'm trying to handle this as best I can? I just don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you ever experienced anything unusual, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't seem to notice?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I really want to assure you, I don't have any... well, anything like hearing things or seeing things that aren't there. I'm completely grounded in reality, I promise. 

I know sometimes when people talk about stress at work, it can sound like things are getting out of hand, but my mind is perfectly clear. I'm just a regular guy trying to do a good job and make sure my reputation stays intact. I hope you believe me when I say that. I would tell you if something like that was happening, really. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever felt certain about something that others have strongly denied or tried to convince you wasn’t true, even though you believed it was very real?

Well, um... I guess that goes back to what I was mentioning a little bit earlier. I hope you don't mind me bringing it up again, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. 

But, yes, it's exactly that situation at work. Like I said, ever since I got that county safety award, I've just been so certain that certain people are twisting my inspection reports. And they ask me those really pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. 

When I finally brought it up to my supervisor, he strongly denied it. He really tried to convince me it was just a normal review process. And, you know, I didn't argue—I agreed with him right then because I always try to be cooperative and I'd hate to cause any trouble. But... even with him saying that, I just know it's very real. I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me, no matter how much they deny it. 

I really hope I don't sound too stubborn or difficult saying that. I just want to be honest with you. Does that kind of fit what you were asking about?

Even though your supervisor told you that the review process is normal, do you still feel certain that people are trying to discredit you, and has that belief stayed strong even though others don’t seem to share it?

Um, yes... I do still feel certain about it. I hope you don't think I'm just being paranoid or... or difficult, because I really do try to get along with everyone. But yes, the belief has stayed very strong. 

It's just... well, like I said, it all started right after I got that county safety award. It's like a switch flipped, you know? And I just can't shake the fact that they are twisting my inspection reports and asking those really specific budget questions to make me look crooked. 

I know my supervisor said it's just a normal review, and I nodded and smiled because I want to be a good employee... but deep down, I can just tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's not that I want to believe it, I just... I know it's happening. I'm sorry if that makes me sound stubborn. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can with you. Is it okay that I feel that way?

Has your belief that people at work are trying to discredit you changed at all since your supervisor told you it was just a normal review process, or has it remained completely unchanged no matter how much others try to reassure you?

Well... honestly, and I really hate to admit this because I know how stubborn it sounds... but no, it hasn't changed. I really, really wish it had. 

When my supervisor told me it was just a normal review, I wanted to just accept it and move on, because I pride myself on being a good team player. But... no matter how much they try to reassure me, I just can't ignore what I'm seeing. Like I was saying, ever since I won that safety award, the way they twist my inspection reports... and the way they ask those budget questions, they’re just so pointed, like they’re trying to catch me in a lie and make me look crooked. 

I don't want to cause any trouble at all, but I just know in my gut there's a coordinated effort to discredit me, even with the reassurances. I'm sorry, I know that probably isn't the right answer, and I hope you don't think I'm just ignoring people's help or being difficult on purpose. I just want to be completely open with you. Is it alright that I still feel that way?

Even though your supervisor and others have told you that this is just a normal review process, do you believe, without any doubt, that their real intention is to discredit you and that they are deliberately twisting your reports?

Well... um, yes. I do. I really hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable, or like I'm trying to be difficult, because I really am not. I just... I want to be honest with you, and the truth is, I don't have any doubt. 

I know they say it's just a normal review, and I always nod and say okay because I don't want to ruffle any feathers. I want them to think I'm doing a good job. But... ever since I got that safety award, it's just so clear to me. The way they twist my inspection reports, and those budget questions... they aren't just normal questions. They're trying to make me look crooked. 

I just know, deep down, that there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm just repeating myself, or if I'm not giving you the answer you're looking for. I just can't pretend it's not happening when I know it is. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
